source_first_reconstruction.statement: For arbitrary natural m,n and arbitrary real m-by-n A, let r=min(m,n). There exist real R of shape m-by-r and Q of shape r-by-n with A=RQ and QQ^T=I_r. No independence, full-rank, positive-dimension, nonzero-row or norm premise is stated. Width r depends on shape, not rank.

nodes.claim: A prefix sum in any additive commutative monoid equals the full finite sum when every complementary term is zero.
nodes.argument: The value-preserving prefix inclusion is injective; sum over its image, then add only zero terms outside it.

nodes.claim: For m<=n, form n vectors in real n-space from the m input rows followed by zero vectors.
A full orthonormal basis obtained by ordered Gram-Schmidt with completion satisfies <b_k,f_i>=0 for i<k even for dependent or zero input vectors.
nodes.argument: Use completion, not a claim that every raw residual has nonzero norm. The ordered zero property is the specific required basis property.
Full orthonormal-basis expansion supplies the first equality. Every discarded k obeys k>=m>i, so the prefix-sum node supplies the second.

nodes.claim: Set R_ik=<b_k,f_i> and Q_kj=(b_k)_j for k<m.
Taking coordinate j in the truncated expansion yields A_ij=sum_{k<m}R_ik Q_kj.
The coordinate inner product of any two retained basis vectors is their Kronecker delta, hence QQ^T=I_m.
If m<=n, substitute min(m,n)=m and use the wide construction. If m>n, substitute min(m,n)=n and use R=A,Q=I_n.

source_first_reconstruction.mathematical_correctness: The argument is valid. For a zero Gram-Schmidt direction, its assigned completion vector is orthogonal to the span of all nonzero normalized directions, hence to every input row; for a nonzero later direction, ordered Gram-Schmidt gives the needed orthogonality to earlier inputs. Consequently completion cannot introduce a nonzero discarded coefficient. The finite sum restriction and real coordinate Gram calculation then establish both equalities. The tall identity branch is exact without any rank condition.

whole_module_comparison.comparison: The public type has arbitrary m,n, AddCommMonoid M, m<=n and exactly the tail-zero premise stated in the lesson. Fin.castLE preserves prefix index values. The actual proof rewrites by the injective image sum and Finset.sum_subset, supplying tail-zero for excluded indices. No positive dimension or stronger additive structure is hidden.

The public hypothesis is solely m<=n in addition to a real input matrix. Witness dimensions m-by-m and m-by-n and the conjunction A=R*Q, Q*Q.transpose=1 exactly match the wide source statement. Local f uses zero-padding and the Euclidean wrapper, b uses a full completion at dimension n, and R uses b.repr. OrthonormalBasis.repr_apply_apply identifies that coefficient with the source inner product. The actual hz proof obtains ordered coefficient zeros, hs restricts the sum, hb expands the basis and evaluates a coordinate, and inner_eq_ite plus PiLp.inner_apply establishes the retained-row identity.

The public type has no shape inequality or extra input assumptions, and both factor widths are exactly min(m,n). The actual case split substitutes min=m and calls the wide theorem, or substitutes min=n and returns A and the identity. This is the same proof topology as the lesson.

boundary_checks.finding: r=0. R is 0-by-0 and Q is 0-by-n; equality and row Gram constraints have no row entries. Prefix restriction also works for an empty prefix.
r=0. R=A is m-by-0 and Q=I_0 is 0-by-0 in the tall route. No column entries or orthonormal rows are required.
Both routes' mathematical contracts are vacuous; the formal split uses the wide route. No division by a zero row norm is required to provide a basis of the zero space.
Q has r genuine unit orthogonal rows supplied by completion; all coefficients in the wide R vanish, or tall R=A=0. The contract does not claim Q itself is zero.

Completion supplies extra directions and the coefficients still reconstruct A. The lesson and formal theorem both use r rows, not rank(A) rows; neither asserts equality of A's row space and Q's row space.
The formal first branch is valid; no nonsingularity premise arises. A square orthogonal Q is possible even when A is singular.
Q=I_n and R=A satisfy the stated equations, but do not provide a triangular/trapezoidal R for arbitrary A. The source expressly denies a triangular-factor conclusion.
QQ^T=I_m is row orthonormality, not Q^TQ=I_n. No silent column-orthonormality or unitary-circuit inference appears.

semantic_slots.target: Match: exact real finite-matrix factorization A=RQ with R:m-by-r,Q:r-by-n,r=min(m,n), and QQ^T=I_r. All three public statements are covered; no triangularity, uniqueness or rank-minimality clause is asserted.
semantic_slots.normalization: Match: Q's rows have real dot products delta_kl, so each existing row has norm one. A and R need no norm bound or normalization. Quantum-state normalization and block-encoding scaling are not applicable because there is no state or block-encoding contract.
semantic_slots.registers: Quantum registers are not applicable: objects are functions on Fin row and column indices. Row index precedes column index, factors use the specified shared width, and ordinary transpose swaps the two indices. No qubit, tensor or endianness convention is present.
semantic_slots.oracles: Not applicable: no oracle-access hypothesis or runtime input API exists. Imported Gram-Schmidt completion and basis theorems are formal proof providers, not quantum or classical access oracles assumed of A.
semantic_slots.ancillas_phases: Not applicable: there is no circuit workspace, ancilla, garbage sector or complex phase. All scalars are real and the theorem uses ordinary transpose; orthonormal-completion choices are noncanonical mathematical witnesses, not relative-phase or cleanup claims.
semantic_slots.error_success: Match: both matrix equations hold exactly, including empty, zero and deficient cases. There is no approximation parameter, numerical stability bound, postselection, randomized procedure or success-probability assertion.
semantic_slots.resources: Match: only output matrix dimensions are asserted. Noncomputable choice-based completion proves existence and does not supply executable stored factors, a numerical algorithm, runtime, query/gate bounds or finite-bit costs. The lesson explicitly preserves those frontiers.
